days.goalUz: Ishlatiladi: tanishish uchun iboralar, to be fe’li (am / is / are), sinf buyumlari va 1–20 sonlari bilan gapirish hamda yozish.

exercises.explanationUz: “sinf xonasi” = classroom.
exercises.question: Which word means "sinf xonasi"?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: sonni inglizcha so‘z bilan yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: 10 + 5 = 15 (fifteen), 9 + 9 = 18 (eighteen).
exercises.text: Ten and five is ___. Nine and nine is ___.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: salomlashish iborasini o‘zbekchaga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: Goodbye — xayr, ko‘rishguncha.
accepted: Xayr, ertaga ko‘rishamiz!
Xayr, ertaga ko‘rishguncha
Ko‘rishguncha, ertaga

exercises.instructionUz: Test: to‘g‘ri grammatik variantni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Ko‘plikdagi “these pencils” bilan are ishlatiladi.
exercises.question: These pencils ___ mine.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 1-kun matnini eslab, fikrga baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Birinci paragrafda bugun dushanba deyilgan.
exercises.statement: Samir writes about a Monday.
exercises.evidence: Today is Monday. I am very happy.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: audioyadagi ma’lumotni eslab, javobni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: O‘qituvchi: See you at eight o’clock.
exercises.question: What time do the students come back to class?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: raqamlarni ularning inglizcha nomlari bilan birlashtiring.
exercises.explanationUz: 7 — seven, 12 — twelve, 15 — fifteen, 20 — twenty.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: so‘zlardan ism haqidagi gapni tartiblab chiqaring.
exercises.explanationUz: To‘g‘ri gap: Her name is Gulnoza.

days.goalUz: Kundalik hayotda oilani tanishtirish: egalik ('s, my/your), have got / has got va odamni tashqi ko‘rinishi bilan tavsiflash.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: testda qarindoshlik atamalarini ma’nosi bilan bog‘lang.
exercises.explanationUz: brother — aka/uka, aunt — xola, parents — ota-ona, hair — soch.

exercises.instructionUz: Testda yosh ifodasini to‘g‘ri variantdan tanlab oling.
exercises.explanationUz: Bibim 70 yoshda: “My grandmother is seventy years old.”
exercises.question: Your grandmother is 70. You say: “My grandmother ...”

exercises.instructionUz: Testda inkor shaklini to‘g‘ri yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Inkor: has not got / hasn’t got.
exercises.text: My uncle ___ a car. He has a bike.

exercises.instructionUz: 2-kun matniga asoslanib, fikrga true / false / notgiven deb baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Ikkinchi paragrafda otaning kasbi aytilmagan — faqat “he is quiet, he has got a bike” deyilgan.
exercises.statement: Dilnoza’s father is a doctor.
exercises.evidence: Ota haqida faqat bo‘yi, xarakteri va velosipedi aytilgan.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: audioda eshitgan ma’lumotni eslab, to‘g‘ri javobni belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: Sardor: “My father is tall and he has got short black hair.”
exercises.question: What has Sardor’s father got?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: o‘zbekcha egalik ifodasini ingliz tiliga aylantiring.
exercises.explanationUz: ‘Otamning velosipedi’ = My father's bike.
accepted: This is my father's bike
This is the bike of my father
It is my father's bike

exercises.instructionUz: Testda so‘roq gapning to‘g‘ri shaklini topib belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: So‘roqda have egadan oldin chiqadi: Has your sister got long hair?
exercises.question: Which question is correct?
options: Has your sister got long hair?
Your sister has got long hair?
Has got your sister long hair?
Is your sister got long hair?

exercises.instructionUz: Testdagi bo‘sh joylarga sifat so‘zlarini qo‘ying.
exercises.explanationUz: tall — baland bo‘yli, young — yosh, tall uchun opposite — short.
exercises.text: My grandfather is not young, he is ___. My brother is not short, he is ___.

days.goalUz: Present Simple yordamida o‘z kunduzini so‘zlab berish: uyanishdan uxlaguncha, hafta kunlari va soatni aytish.

sections.titleUz: Yangi so‘zlar: kunlik tartib va vaqt
Grammatika: Present Simple va vaqt prepozitsiyalari

exercises.instructionUz: Test: so‘zma-so‘z aytilgan vaqtni raqamli shaklga bog‘lang.
exercises.explanationUz: half past seven = 7:30, a quarter past eight = 8:15, a quarter to nine = 8:45.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: vaqt prepozitsiyalarini to‘g‘ri qo‘ying.
exercises.explanationUz: Soat — at, hafta kuni — on, kunduz qismi — in.
exercises.text: School starts ___ eight o’clock. We have an English lesson ___ Monday. I do my homework ___ the afternoon.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: uchinchi shaxs shakli qo‘llangan gapni toping.
exercises.explanationUz: My sister — uchinchi shaxs yagona: watches.
exercises.question: My sister ___ TV in the evening.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: otangiz haqidagi gapni so‘zlar bilan tuzib chiqing.
exercises.explanationUz: To‘g‘ri gap: My father gets up at half past five.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: audioyadagi ma’lumotga suyangan holda baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: “In the evening I do my homework and I play tennis with my sister.”
exercises.statement: Bekzod does his homework in the evening.
exercises.evidence: In the evening I do my homework and I play tennis with my sister.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: o‘qilgan matndan bir savolga javob toping.
exercises.explanationUz: “We have lunch at twelve o’clock at school.”
exercises.question: Where does Aziza have lunch?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: hafta kunlarining nomlarini inglizcha yozing.
exercises.explanationUz: Biz dushanbadan juma rigacha o‘qiymiz: Monday. Dam olish kunlari — Saturday, Sunday.
exercises.text: We have lessons from ___ to Friday. The weekend days are ___ and ___.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: soat so‘rovi haqidagi o‘zbekcha gapni inglizchaga aylantiring.
exercises.explanationUz: uxlashga bormoq = go to bed; “soat to‘qqizda” = at nine o’clock; “kechqurun” = in the evening.
accepted: He goes to bed at nine o’clock in the evening
He goes to bed at nine o'clock in the evening
He goes to bed at nine in the evening
He sleeps at nine o’clock in the evening
She goes to bed at nine o’clock in the evening

days.goalUz: Ishlatiladi: uy-xona so‘zlari (house, kitchen, bedroom ...), “There is / There are“ va in / on / under / next to predloglari bilan joyini aytish.

sections.titleUz: Yangi so‘zlar: uy, xonalar va joy predloglari
Grammatika: There is / There are va joy predloglari

exercises.instructionUz: Test: ovqat pishiriladigan xonani inglizcha belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: “oshxona“ = kitchen.
exercises.question: Which word means "oshxona"?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: bo‘sh joyga to‘g‘ri predlogni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: Yostiq karavot ustida — on (“ustida“).
exercises.question: The pillow is ___ the bed.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: to‘g‘ri grammatik shaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: “three lamps“ ko‘plik, shuning uchun There are.
exercises.question: ___ three lamps in the shop.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: bo‘sh joylarni to‘g‘ri so‘zlar bilan to‘ldiring.
exercises.explanationUz: Bitta deraza — is; “two doors“ — are; “two doors“ yozilishi "two".
exercises.text: There ___ one window in my room. There ___ two doors. Two and one is ___.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 4-kun o‘qish matnini eslab, fikrga baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Matnda oshxona vanna xonasi yonida deyilgan.
exercises.statement: The kitchen is next to the bathroom.
exercises.evidence: The kitchen is next to the bathroom.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 4-kun tinglash matniga asoslanib baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Transkriptda oshxonada ovqat bor deyilgan, stullar soni esa 4 ta.
exercises.statement: There are four chairs in the kitchen.
exercises.evidence: This is the kitchen. There are four chairs and a big table in it.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: so‘zlarni tartib bilan qo‘ying.
exercises.explanationUz: To‘g‘ri gap: Is there a bathroom in your flat?
exercises.noteUz: Eslatma: so‘zlar orasiga "?" qo‘yish shart emas.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: gapni inglizchaga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Mehmonxonada katta divan bor“ = There is a big sofa in the living room.
accepted: There is a big sofa in the living room
There’s a big sofa in the living room
There is a big sofa in the living room.

days.titleUz: Ovqat va ichimliklar: birozmi, yoki yo‘qmi?
days.goalUz: Ishlatiladi: ovqat va ichimlik so‘zlari, “some / any“ hamda sanaladigan–sanalmaydigan ismlar, “I like cooking“ kabi “like + -ing“ gaplar.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: “chanqagan“ so‘zining inglizchasini belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: thirsty — chanqagan; hungry — och.
exercises.question: Which word means "chanqagan"?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: bo‘sh joyga to‘g‘ri so‘zni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: So‘roq gapda any ishlatiladi.
exercises.question: Are there ___ bananas in the bag?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: qaysi gap to‘g‘ri?
exercises.explanationUz: “water“ sanalmaydigan, shuning uchun isn’t any.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: There aren’t any waters in the glass.
There isn’t any water in the glass.
There isn’t any waters in the glass.
There are any water in the glass.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: bo‘sh joylarni to‘ldiring.
exercises.explanationUz: like’den keyin cooking; tasdiqda some; inkorda any.
exercises.text: My father enjoys ___ dinner. There is ___ bread on the table. There isn’t ___ tea in the cup.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 5-kun o‘qish matnini eslab, baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Matnda guruch, go‘sht va tuxum sotib olingan; sut esa xarid qilinmagan.
exercises.statement: The family buys rice and meat at the market.
exercises.evidence: We buy two kilos of rice, some meat and ten eggs.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 5-kun tinglash matniga asoslanib baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Malika och (hungry) ekanini aytadi; chanqaganligi esa NECHA to‘g‘ri necha noto‘g‘ri ekanini audio aytmaydi — Not Given.
exercises.statement: Malika is thirsty at first.
exercises.evidence: Good morning! I am hungry. Is there any bread for breakfast?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: so‘zlarni to‘g‘ri tartibda qo‘ying.
exercises.explanationUz: To‘g‘ri gap: I like eating apples with my sister.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: gapni inglizchaga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Oshxonada biroz non bor“ = There is some bread in the kitchen.
accepted: There is some bread in the kitchen
There’s some bread in the kitchen
There is some bread in the kitchen.

days.titleUz: Bo‘sh vaqt, qiziqishlar va hafta oxiri rejalari
days.goalUz: Ishlatiladi: bo‘sh vaqt va havas so‘zlari, “can / can’t“ bilan qobiliyat, “am / is / are going to“ bilan yakshanba rejalari.

sections.titleUz: Yangi so‘zlar: bo‘sh vaqt va qiziqishlar
Grammatika: can / can’t va going to
O‘qish: “Bo‘sh vaqtim va dam olish kunim“

exercises.instructionUz: Test: “kinoteatr“ so‘zining inglizchasini belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: cinema — kinoteatr.
exercises.question: Which word means "kinoteatr"?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: to‘g‘ri shaklni tanlang.
exercises.explanationUz: “can“dan keyin fe’l o‘z shaklida — sing.
exercises.question: My sister can ___ three English songs.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: reja haqidagi to‘g‘ri gapni belgilang.
exercises.explanationUz: “he“ bilan is going to ishlatiladi.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: He is going to swim on Sunday.
He going to swim on Sunday.
He goes to swim on Sunday.
He is going swim on Sunday.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: bo‘sh joylarni to‘ldiring.
exercises.explanationUz: Iloj bor — can, yo‘q — can’t; reja — am going to.
exercises.text: I ___ dance, but I ___ swim. On Sunday I ___ going to ride a bike.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 6-kun o‘qish matnini eslab, baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Matnda bog‘da basketbol maydoni bor deyilgan, suzish havzasi aytilmagan.
exercises.statement: There is a basketball court in the park.
exercises.evidence: There is a small lake in the park, and there is a court for basketball next to it.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 6-kun tinglash matniga asoslanib baho bering.
exercises.explanationUz: Farrukh filmni amakivachchasi (cousin — amaki yoki toqaning farzandi) bilan ko‘rmoqchi.
exercises.statement: Farrukh is going to watch a film with his cousin on Sunday.
exercises.evidence: On Sunday I am going to watch a film with my cousin. Do you want to come?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: so‘zlarni to‘g‘ri tartibda qo‘ying.
exercises.explanationUz: To‘g‘ri gap: Are you going to play basketball this weekend?

exercises.instructionUz: Test: gapni inglizchaga tarjima qiling.
exercises.explanationUz: “Men ertaga kinoteatrga bormoqchiman“ = I am going to the cinema ...
accepted: I am going to the cinema tomorrow
I’m going to the cinema tomorrow
I want to go to the cinema tomorrow
I’d like to go to the cinema tomorrow

days.titleUz: Sayohat, yo‘l so‘rash va hafta yakuniy takrori
days.goalUz: Ishlatiladi: transport va sayohat so‘zlari, yo‘l so‘rash (How do I get to ...?, Turn left), “was / were“ bilan kechagi joylar — keyin butun hafta takrori testi.

sections.titleUz: Yangi so‘zlar: transport, bekat va yo‘l belgilari
Grammatika: yo‘l so‘rash va was / were
Gapirish: transport, yo‘l ko‘rsatish, kechagi joylar

exercises.instructionUz: Test: to‘g‘ri fe’l shaklini belgilang (1-kun: to be).
exercises.explanationUz: “She“ — uchinchi shaxs yagona, shuning uchun is.
exercises.question: She ___ a teacher and I ___ her student.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: oila a’zosi so‘zini tanlang (2-kun: family).
exercises.explanationUz: Amaki yoki toqaning qizi/o‘g‘li ingliz tilida “cousin“ deyiladi.
exercises.question: My uncle’s daughter is my ___.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: kunlik tartib haqidagi gaplarni to‘ldiring (3-kun: present simple).
exercises.explanationUz: I bilan get / have ishlatiladi — present simple, shaxsga -s qo‘shilmaydi.
exercises.text: Every morning I ___ up at half past six. Then I ___ breakfast with my family at seven o’clock.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: joy va “there is/are“ (4-kun).
exercises.explanationUz: “two buses“ ko‘plik — There are; bekat esa binoning YONIDA — next to.
exercises.question: ___ two buses at the stop, and the stop is ___ our building.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: gapni o‘zbekchaga tarjima qiling (5-kun: some / any).
exercises.explanationUz: He isn’t thirsty — “u chanqagan emas“; inkor gapda any keladi — “suv ham xohlamaydi“.
exercises.source: He isn’t thirsty, and he doesn’t want any water.
accepted: U chanqagan emas va u hech qanday suv xohlamaydi
U chanqagan emas, unga suv kerak emas
U chanqoq emas va suv xohlamaydi
U chanqagan emas va u suv ham xohlamaydi
U chanqoq emas, unga suv ham kerak emas

exercises.instructionUz: Test: so‘zlarni to‘g‘ri qo‘yib, reja haqidagi gap tuzing (6-kun: going to).
exercises.explanationUz: To‘g‘ri gap: We are going to visit the museum next Sunday.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: 7-kun o‘qish matniga asoslanib baho bering (was / were).
exercises.explanationUz: Matnda “on Sunday morning we were in Samarkand“ deyilgan, shuning uchun fikr to‘g‘ri.
exercises.statement: The family was in Samarkand on Sunday morning.
exercises.evidence: We were on a big train for three hours, and on Sunday morning we were in Samarkand.

exercises.instructionUz: Test: yo‘l ko‘rsatish gapini inglizchaga tarjima qiling (7-kun).
exercises.explanationUz: Chapga buriling = Turn left; to‘g‘ri boring = go straight ahead.
accepted: Turn left and go straight ahead
Turn left and go straight
Turn left and go straight ahead.

vocab.explanationEn: You say this when you meet someone.
vocab.exampleEn: Hello, my name is Samir.

vocab.explanationEn: You say this when you leave.
vocab.exampleEn: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!

vocab.explanationEn: A word for a person, a city or a thing.
vocab.exampleEn: What is your name?

vocab.explanationEn: The start of the day, before twelve o’clock.
vocab.exampleEn: Good morning! I am late.

vocab.explanationEn: A room where students have lessons.
vocab.exampleEn: Our classroom is big and clean.
vocab.exampleUz: Bizning sinf xonamiz katta va toza.

vocab.explanationEn: A person who studies at a school or a university.
vocab.exampleEn: I am a student at School Number Seven.

vocab.explanationEn: A person whose job is teaching people.
vocab.exampleEn: Our English teacher is very kind.
vocab.exampleUz: Bizning ingliz tili o‘qituvchimiz juda mehribon.

vocab.explanationEn: You read a book. It has many pages.
vocab.exampleEn: This book has twenty pages.

vocab.explanationEn: A tool for writing with ink.
vocab.exampleEn: Is this your pen or my pen?

vocab.explanationEn: A tool for writing. You can erase a pencil.
vocab.exampleEn: I have a new pencil and an eraser.
vocab.exampleUz: Menda yangi qalam va o‘chirg‘ich bor.

vocab.explanationEn: A table for one student at school.
vocab.exampleEn: There are twenty desks in our classroom.

vocab.explanationEn: A word like one, two, ten or twenty.
vocab.exampleEn: My number is seven and my age is eleven.
vocab.exampleUz: Mening raqamim yetti, yoshim o‘n bir.

vocab.explanationEn: The people you live with: parents, brothers and sisters.
vocab.exampleEn: My family has five people.

vocab.explanationEn: Your mother and your father together.
vocab.exampleEn: My parents are teachers.

vocab.explanationEn: A girl with the same mother and father as you.
vocab.exampleEn: My sister Nilufar is fifteen.

vocab.explanationEn: A boy with the same mother and father as you.
vocab.exampleEn: My brother Sanjar is eight years old.

vocab.explanationEn: The mother of your mother or your father.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandmother is seventy years old.

vocab.explanationEn: The father of your mother or your father.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather has a small garden.

vocab.explanationEn: The sister of your mother or your father.
vocab.exampleEn: My aunt has two sons.

vocab.explanationEn: The son or daughter of your aunt or uncle.
vocab.exampleEn: My cousin is eleven and he is tall.
vocab.exampleUz: Amakivachcham o‘n bir yoshda, u baland bo‘yli.

vocab.explanationEn: Not short. Your father can be tall.
vocab.exampleEn: My father is tall and kind.

vocab.explanationEn: Not tall. Also: not long, like a short book.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandmother is short and quiet.
vocab.exampleUz: Bibim bo‘yiga past va xulqi tinch.

vocab.explanationEn: Not old. A young person is fourteen, for example.
vocab.exampleEn: The students in my class are young.

vocab.explanationEn: The soft thing that grows on your head.
vocab.exampleEn: She has long black hair.

vocab.explanationEn: To stop sleeping in the morning.
vocab.exampleEn: I wake up at six thirty.

vocab.explanationEn: To leave your bed after you wake up.
vocab.exampleEn: I get up fast and put on my uniform.

vocab.explanationEn: The first food of your day, in the morning.
vocab.exampleEn: I have breakfast with my family.

vocab.explanationEn: You do this to your teeth every morning.
vocab.exampleEn: I brush my teeth every morning.

vocab.explanationEn: Special clothes that all students in a school wear.
vocab.exampleEn: My school uniform is blue and white.
vocab.exampleUz: Mening maktab formam ko‘k va oq.

vocab.explanationEn: The food you eat in the middle of the day.
vocab.exampleEn: We have lunch at twelve o’clock.

vocab.explanationEn: A thing you study at school, like maths or English.
vocab.exampleEn: My favourite subject is English.

vocab.explanationEn: School work that the teacher gives you for home.
vocab.exampleEn: I do my homework at half past four.
vocab.exampleUz: Uy vazifamni soat to‘rt yarimda qilaman.

vocab.explanationEn: Most of the time, but not always.
vocab.exampleEn: I usually drink tea for breakfast.

vocab.explanationEn: Saturday and Sunday. You do not go to school.
vocab.exampleEn: On the weekend I get up late.

vocab.explanationEn: We say it for a full hour: at six o’clock.
vocab.exampleEn: School starts at eight o’clock.

vocab.explanationEn: Before the usual time. Early is the opposite of late.
vocab.exampleEn: I go to bed early on Sunday.

vocab.explanationEn: A building where a family lives.
vocab.exampleEn: Our house is small but warm.

vocab.explanationEn: A part of a house with walls and a door.
vocab.exampleEn: There are five rooms in our flat.

vocab.explanationEn: The room where people cook food.
vocab.exampleEn: My mother cooks dinner in the kitchen.

vocab.explanationEn: A room where you sleep.
vocab.exampleEn: My bedroom is small and clean.
vocab.exampleUz: Mening yotish xonam kichik va toza.

vocab.explanationEn: A room where you wash and take a bath.
vocab.exampleEn: The bathroom is next to the kitchen.

vocab.explanationEn: A room where a family sits together in the evening.
vocab.exampleEn: The TV is in the living room.

vocab.explanationEn: A part of a wall with glass. You look outside through it.
vocab.exampleEn: There are two windows in the kitchen.

vocab.explanationEn: You put things on it and eat at it.
vocab.exampleEn: There are two books on the table.

vocab.explanationEn: You sit on it.
vocab.exampleEn: The chair is next to the table.

vocab.explanationEn: You sleep on it at night.
vocab.exampleEn: My bed is soft and clean.

vocab.explanationEn: Below something, with the thing over it.
vocab.exampleEn: The cat sleeps under the chair.

vocab.explanationEn: At the side of something, very near it.
vocab.exampleEn: The lamp is next to the window.

vocab.explanationEn: Food made from flour. You cannot count it.
vocab.exampleEn: There is some bread on the table.

vocab.explanationEn: Small white grains you cook and eat.
vocab.exampleEn: We sometimes have rice and meat for lunch.
vocab.exampleUz: Tushlikda ba’zan guruch va go‘sht eymiz.

vocab.explanationEn: You can count eggs: one egg, two eggs.
vocab.exampleEn: There are two eggs in the fridge.

vocab.explanationEn: A round fruit. You can count apples.
vocab.exampleEn: I eat an apple every day.

vocab.explanationEn: A white food made from milk. It is uncountable.
vocab.exampleEn: There isn’t any cheese at home.

vocab.explanationEn: A white drink from a cow. You cannot count it.
vocab.exampleEn: I drink warm milk at night.

vocab.explanationEn: You drink it every day. It is uncountable.
vocab.exampleEn: Can I have some water, please?

vocab.explanationEn: Food that comes from an animal.
vocab.exampleEn: My uncle does not eat any meat.

vocab.explanationEn: You put food in your mouth.
vocab.exampleEn: I eat soup for dinner.

grammar.titleUz: To be fe’li: am / is / are
grammar.titleEn: The verb to be: am / is / are
explanationUz: Ingliz tilida “men talabaman”, “u o‘qituvchi”, “biz do‘stmiz” deganda “to be” fe’li ishlatiladi. O‘zbek tilida bunday gapda fe’l bo‘lmaydi, ingliz tilida esa fe’l albatta kerak: I am a student, She is a teacher. Fe’lsiz gap ingliz tilida xato hisoblanadi.

To be fe’li shaxsga qarab uch shaklga ega: I bilan am ishlatiladi; he, she, it va yagona narsa bilan is; we, you, they va ko‘plikdagi narsalar bilan are. Eslab qolish uchun uchta qatorni takrorlang: I am — you are — he is / she is / it is — we are — they are.

Inkor gapda to be fe’lidan keyin not qo‘yiladi: I am not late. She is not (isn’t) a teacher. They are not (aren’t) in the classroom. So‘roq gapda esa to be fe’li ega oldinga chiqadi: Are you a student? — Yes, I am. / No, I am not. Is her name Aziza? — Yes, it is.

So‘zlashuvda qisqartmalar juda ko‘p ishlatiladi: I’m, she’s, he’s, they’re, we’re. Inkorda esa isn’t, aren’t, ‘m not shakllari uchraydi. Yozma testlarda qisqartma va to‘liq shakl ikkalasi ham to‘g‘ri javobdir, lekin bitta gapda fe’lni ikki marta qaytarish xato: “I am a student, am a teacher” deb yozilmaydi.

grammar.titleUz: Egalik: ’s, my / your va have got
grammar.titleEn: Possessives: ’s, my / your, and have got
explanationUz: Narsa kimniki ekanini aytish uchun ingliz tilida ismga ’s qo‘shiladi: Bekzod’s book (Bekzodning kitobi), my sister’s bag (singilmning sumkasi). Agar egalardan bir nechta bo‘lsa va ular bir narsaga tegishli bo‘lsa, ’s oxirgi ismga qo‘yiladi: Aziz and Malika’s home. Egalik “of” bilan ham aytiladi, lekin A1 darajasida ’s eng tabiiy yo‘ldir.

my, your, his, her, our, their so‘zlari “kimniki” degan savolga javob beradi va har doim ot oldida keladi: my book, your pen, his name, her hair, our class, their friends. Bu so‘zlar o‘zi egalikni bildiradi, ularga ’s qo‘shilmaydi: “my book” (hech qachon “my’s book” emas). Javobda otni takrorlamaslik ham mumkin: “Is this your pen?” — “Yes, it is my pen.”

Biror narsaga ega ekanlikni have got bilan aytkazamiz: I have got a bike. She has got two brothers. Uchinchi shaxs yagonada has ishlatilishini unutmang. Inkor: I haven’t got a phone. She hasn’t got a bike. So‘roq: Have you got a pen? Has he got a red bag? Qisqartmalar so‘zlashuvda ko‘p: I’ve got, she’s got, he hasn’t got.

Odamni tasvirlashda ham have got ishlatiladi: He has got short black hair. She has got blue eyes. Sifatlar ot oldida keladi va ko‘plikda o‘zgarmaydi: two tall boys (tall so‘ziga -lar qo‘shilmaydi). Kasb, yosh va kayfiyat esa to be fe’li bilan aytiladi: She is a teacher. He is eight. Bu ikki tuzilmani aralashtirmang: egalik — have got, sifat, kasb va yosh — to be.

grammar.titleEn: Present Simple and talking about time
explanationUz: Har kuni takrorlanadigan ishlarimizni Present Simple zamoni bilan aytamiz: I get up at six. She goes to school at eight. Bu zamon “men odatda shunday qilaman” degan ma’noni beradi, shuning uchun “every day”, “usually”, “never”, “on Monday” kabi so‘zlar ko‘p ishlatiladi.

Ega uchinchi shaxs yagona bo‘lsa (he, she, it, my mother, Bekzod), fe’l olga -s yoki -es qo‘shadi: he plays, she goes, he watches, she has. “have” → “has”, “go” → “goes”, “do” → “does” shakllarini alohida eslab qolish kerak. Boshqa shaxslarda fe’l o‘zgarmaydi: I play, you play, we play, they play.

Inkor va so‘roq gaplarda yordamchi fe’l do / does keladi va asosiy fe’l -siz qoladi: I do not (don’t) watch TV. He does not (doesn’t) get up late. Do you go to school by bus? Does she like English? “He doesn’t goes” deb ikki marta -s qo‘yilmaydi.

Vaqt bildirishda prepozitsiyalarni chalkashtirmang: soat bilan — at (at eight o’clock, at half past six); hafta kuni bilan — on (on Monday, on Friday); kunduz qismlari bilan — in (in the morning, in the evening). “half past six” — oltidan yarim o‘tgan, 6:30; “a quarter past seven” — 7:15; “a quarter to nine” — sakkizdan chorak qoldi, 8:45. Kunlar katta harf bilan yoziladi: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

grammar.titleUz: There is / there are va joy bildiruvchi predloglar
grammar.titleEn: There is / there are and prepositions of place
explanationUz: Uyda yoki xonada biror narsa borligini aytish uchun ingliz tilida “there is” va “there are” ishlatiladi. Bitta narsa uchun there is, ikki yoki undan ko‘p narsa uchun there are qo‘llanadi. O‘zbekchadagi “bor” so‘zi bu yerda fe’l shakliga qarab ikki xil bo‘ladi: There is a bed. / There are two beds.

There is ko‘pincha qisqartirilib “there’s” deyiladi: There’s a lamp in my room. Inkor shakli — there is not (there isn’t) va there are not (there aren’t): There isn’t a TV in my room. There aren’t any chairs in the kitchen.

Narsa qayerda turishini bildirish uchun in, on, under, next to predloglari ishlatiladi. “in” — ichida: in the kitchen, in the box. “on” — ustida: on the table, on the wall. “under” — ostida: under the bed. “next to” — yonida: next to the door.

Bu gap tartibi o‘zbekchadan farq qiladi. O‘zbekchada joy so‘zi gapning oxirida keladi (“Kitob stol ustida“), ingliz tilida esa predlog to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri fe’ldan (is / are) keyin keladi: The book is on the table. Shuning uchun “The book is” deb qoldirmang, joy albatta aytiladi.

So‘roq qurish uchun is yoki are egadan oldinga chiqadi: Is there a bathroom in your flat? Are there windows in the kitchen? Qisqa javoblar: Yes, there is. / No, there isn’t. / Yes, there are. / No, there aren’t.

formula.form: There is + a / an + bitta narsa
formula.noteUz: Bitta narsa uchun: There is a sofa in the living room.
Ikki yoki undan ko‘p: There are four chairs in the kitchen.

formula.form: There is not (isn’t) / There are not (aren’t)
formula.noteUz: Inkor uchun not qo‘shiladi: There isn’t a lamp here.
So‘roqda is/are oldinga chiqadi.

formula.noteUz: The cat is under the table.

grammar.titleUz: Some / any, sanaladigan va sanalmaydigan ismlar, like + -ing
grammar.titleEn: Some / any, countable and uncountable nouns, like + -ing
explanationUz: Ovqat va ichimliklar haqida gapirganda “biroz / bir necha“ ma’nosida some ishlatiladi. Some tasdiq gaplarda keladi va ham sanaladigan, ham sanalmaydigan ism bilan ishlaydi: There is some bread on the table. There are some eggs in the fridge.

Inkor va so‘roq gaplarda esa any ishlatiladi: There isn’t any milk. Are there any apples? Any ham sanaladigan ko‘plik, ham sanalmaydigan ism bilan keladi. Ruxsat so‘rash yoki taklif qilishda esa some ishlatiladi: Can I have some water? Would you like some tea?

Ingliz tilida ismlar ikki turga bo‘linadi. Sanaladigan ismlar bitta va ko‘plik shaklga ega: an apple — two apples, an egg — three eggs. Ulardan oldin a/an qo‘yiladi va ko‘plikda -s qo‘shiladi. Sanalmaydigan ismlar (bread, rice, water, milk, cheese, meat) hech qachon -s olamaydi va ular bilan “is“ ishlatiladi: The rice is hot. There is some rice in the box.

Miqdor so‘rashda how many sanaladigan ko‘plik bilan, how much esa sanalmaydigan ism bilan keladi: How many eggs do we need? How much water do you drink? Sanalmaydigan ism miqdori idish orqali aytiladi: a glass of water, a cup of tea, a kilo of rice.

Biror narsani yoqtirishni aytishda like va enjoy’den keyin fe’l -ing shaklida keladi: I like cooking. My parents enjoy eating together. Inkor shakl — like’ni don’t / doesn’t bilan: I don’t like soup. She doesn’t like cooking fish.

grammar.titleUz: Can / can’t (qila olish, qo‘l kelish) va “going to“ bilan reja
grammar.titleEn: Can / can’t for ability and “going to“ for plans
explanationUz: Biror ishni bila olish yoki qila olishni aytish uchun “can“ ishlatiladi. “Can“dan keyin fe’l doim o‘z shaklida keladi: hech qanday -s, -ing yoki “to“ qo‘shilmaydi. I can swim. She can play the guitar. He can ride a bike.

Qila olmaslikni “can’t“ (can not) bilan aytamiz: I can’t swim. My brother can’t dance. So‘roqda “can“ egadan oldin chiqadi: Can you dance? Can your sister sing? Qisqa javoblar: Yes, I can. / No, I can’t.
“Can“dan keyingi fe’l shaxsga qarab o‘zgarmasligini esda saqlang: “She cans“, “He can plays“ deyilmaydi. To‘g‘ri: She can sing, he can sing. Bu qoida boshqa fe’llardan farq qiladi.

Kelasi hafta yoki yakshanba uchun rejangiz borligini aytishda “be + going to“ ishlatiladi: I am going to watch a film. We are going to play football in the park. Bu yerda “am / is / are“ shaxsga mos tanlanadi: I am, he/she/it is, we/you/they are.

Reja haqidagi so‘roqda “am / is / are“ egadan oldinga chiqadi: What are you going to do on Saturday? Where is she going to play? Inkor uchun not qo‘shiladi: I am not going to stay at home. Rejalar ko‘pincha aniq vaqt bilan keladi: on Saturday, at nine o’clock, this weekend.

grammar.titleEn: Asking for directions and was / were
explanationUz: Biror joyga qanday borishni so‘rash uchun “Excuse me, how do I get to ...?” deyiladi. Javobda yo‘l ko‘rsatish gaplari ishlatiladi: “Go straight ahead“ — to‘g‘ri boring; “Turn left“ — chapga buriling; “Turn right“ — o‘ngga buriling. Joy yaqin yoki uzoq ekanini “It is near“ va “It is far“ bilan aytamiz.

Yo‘l ko‘rsatishda 4-kundagi joy predloglari yana kerak bo‘ladi: “The station is next to the gate“, “The bus stop is in front of the shop“, “The crossing is under the bridge“. Shuning uchun yo‘l so‘rash mavzusi oldingi kunlar bilan bevosita bog‘langan.

Kechagi yoki oldingi biror joyda bo‘lganimizni aytish uchun “to be“ fe’lining o‘tgan zamoni — was va were — ishlatiladi. “I was, he was, she was, it was“; “we were, you were, they were“. O‘zbekchadagi “... edim / ... edik“ shu ikki shaklga to‘g‘ri keladi: I was at home. We were at the station.

Inkor shakli: was not (wasn’t) va were not (weren’t): I wasn’t at the airport. They weren’t in the train. So‘roqda was / were egadan oldinga chiqadi: Where were you yesterday? Was the museum interesting? Qisqa javob: Yes, I was. / No, I wasn’t.

“Was / were“ faqat bitta holat yoki joy haqida ishlatiladi, harakat fe’llari bilan emas. A1 darajasida “I was happy“, “We were in Samarkand“ kabi gaplar yetarli. Harakatni esa “We went ...“ yoki “We were on a train“ kabi sodda iboralar bilan ifodalaymiz.

paragraphs: My name is Dilnoza and I am thirteen years old. I live in Tashkent with my family. My family is not big: there are five people in it — my mother, my father, my little brother, my grandmother and me.

My mother's name is Malika. She is thirty-two and she is a teacher. She is tall and she has got long black hair. My father's name is Rustam. He is thirty-five. He is short, he is quiet, and he has got a blue bike.

My little brother is Sanjar. He is eight years old and he has got a big red bag. My grandmother lives with us. Her hair is short and grey and she is very kind. Our home is small, but our family is warm. I love my family.

reading.title: My Day, Hour by Hour
paragraphs: My name is Aziza and I am twelve years old. I wake up at half past six every morning. First I brush my teeth and wash my face. Then I have breakfast with my family. I usually drink hot tea and eat bread with cheese.

I put on my school uniform and walk to school. School starts at eight o’clock and I am never late. My favourite subject is English. I also like maths and art. We have lunch at twelve o’clock at school, and school finishes at two o’clock. I come home with my friend Nilufar.

In the afternoon I do my homework. It is often difficult, but I like it. At half past five I play tennis with my brother or I draw a picture. We have dinner together at half past eight. I go to bed at nine o’clock and sleep nine hours. On Saturday and Sunday I do not get up early — I sleep until ten!

paragraphs: I live in a flat in Tashkent with my family. My flat is not big, but it is warm and clean. There are five rooms: a living room, two bedrooms, a kitchen and a bathroom. The kitchen is next to the bathroom.
My favourite room is my bedroom. There is a bed, a small table and a lamp in my bedroom. My books are on the table, and my school bag is under the chair. A picture of my family is on the wall.

In the living room there is a soft sofa and a TV. In the evening my family sits there together. My little brother often plays under the table. There are no computers in our rooms, because my mother says: “Games are not good for you.”

reading.title: Food for the Weekend
paragraphs: On Saturday morning I go to the market near my house with my mother. We need some food for the weekend. We buy two kilos of rice, some meat and ten eggs. The market is big and there are a lot of people there.

At home we put the food on the table. There isn’t any milk in the fridge, so my father goes to the small shop near our building. I like cooking, so I make soup and a salad. Are there any apples in the bag? Yes, there are five apples!

In the evening my family eats together at the big table. My little sister drinks tea with sugar, but she doesn’t like soup. My parents enjoy eating with our neighbours, so we invite them on Sunday. Food is always better with friends.

paragraphs: My name is Sardor and I am thirteen. I like my free time because I can do the things I love. I can play football very well, and I can ride a bike for two hours. My sister can dance, but she can’t swim.

paragraphs: Tashkent is a big city. There are many buses and a metro here, and there is a long bridge over the river. I go to school by bus every day, because the bus stop is next to our building and a ticket is cheap.

Last weekend was different. On Saturday my family and I were at the railway station in Tashkent. We were on a big train for three hours, and on Sunday morning we were in Samarkand. My little sister was very happy, because she saw a big square and very old buildings.

In the city, I asked a man, “Excuse me, how do I get to the museum?” He said, “Go straight ahead and turn left at the crossing. The museum is next to the blue gate.” We were at the museum in five minutes. The museum was old and very interesting.

writing.promptEn: Write a short email to your new English class. Say your name, your age, your school and the things you have in your bag.
writing.instructionUz: Yangi ingliz tili sinfingizga qisqa xat yozing. O‘zingizni tanishtiring: ismingiz, yoshingiz, maktabingiz va sumkangizda narsalar borligini ayting. To be fe’lini (am / is / are) kamida uch marta ishlatishga harakat qiling.
checklistUz: Xat boshlanishi va oxiri bor (Hello ... / Goodbye ...).
Ismingiz va yoshingiz to‘g‘ri yozilgan.
To be fe’li kamida uch marta ishlatilgan.
Sumkangizdagi ikkita buyum nomlangan.
Gaplar katta harf bilan boshlanib, nuqta bilan tugatilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Tanishtirish uchun “My name is ...” iborasi albatta kerak.
Yosh, maktab va his-tuyg‘u “I am ...” bilan aytiladi.
Sinf buyumlari mavzusini ochish uchun sumkadagi narsalar sanaladi.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hello! My name is Aziza. I am twelve years old and I am a student at School Number Five. My classroom is big. I have two books, a pen and a pencil in my bag. I am happy to meet you. Thank you! Goodbye, Aziza.

writing.promptEn: Write a short message to your English friend about your family. Say how many people there are, describe one person (age, hair, tall or short) and one thing he or she has got.
writing.instructionUz: Do‘stingizga inglizcha qisqa xabar yozing: oilangizda nechta kishi borligini ayting, bitta oila a’zosini tavsiflang (yoshi, sochi, bo‘yi) va uning nimaga ega ekanligini have got bilan ko‘rsating.
checklistUz: Oiladagi kishilar soni angliycha son bilan yozilgan.
Bitta kishining yoshi va tashqi ko‘rinishi bor.
have got / has got kamida bitta marta ishlatilgan.
Egalik shakli ('s yoki my/your) kamida bitta marta ishlatilgan.
Xabar salom bilan boshlanib, do‘stona tamomlangan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Mavzuga kirish uchun “My family has ...” gap kerak.
Egalik va tavsifda has / have got shakli ishlatilishi talab qilinadi.
Tavsif obyekti aniq bo‘lishi uchun yaqin qarindosh tanlanadi.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Aziza! My family has five people: my mother, my father, my little brother, my grandmother and me. My mother’s name is Malika. She is thirty-two and she is tall. She has got long black hair. My father has got a blue bike. I love my family! See you at school, Dilnoza.

writing.promptEn: Write a paragraph about your day. Say what time you wake up, get up and go to school. Say what you do in the afternoon and what time you go to bed.
writing.instructionUz: Bir kuningiz haqida paragraf yozing: nechida uyanishingiz, o‘rnidan turishingiz va maktabga borishingizni ayting. Kunduzdan keyin nima qilishingiz va nechida uxlashga yotishingizni yozing. Present Simple ishlatib, vaqtni at bilan ko‘rsating.
checklistUz: Kamida uchta vaqt ko‘rsatilgan (uyonish, maktab, uxlash).
Present Simple fe’llari to‘g‘ri ishlatilgan (I go, I do, I have).
at + soat qoidasi saqlangan.
Kunduzdan keyingi bir faoliyat aytilgan.
Paragraf bitta butun matn bo‘lib, nuqtalar qo‘yilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Kunlik tartibni boshlash uchun “I wake up at ...” gap kerak.
Kunni tugatish uchun “I go to bed at ...” gapini yozish kerak.
Kun davomiy ko‘rsatilsin deb kunduzgi faoliyat sanaladi.

writing.modelAnswerEn: I wake up at half past six and I get up fast. I brush my teeth and I have breakfast at seven o’clock. I go to school at eight o’clock. School finishes at two o’clock and I come home. In the afternoon I do my homework and I play tennis with my brother. I go to bed at nine o’clock and I sleep nine hours.

writing.promptEn: Write about your home. How many rooms are there? What is in your favourite room, and where are the things?
writing.instructionUz: O‘z uyingiz haqida inglizcha matn yozing. Xonalar sonini ayting, sevimli xonangizni tanlang va undagi narsalarning joyini “there is / there are“ hamda in / on / under / next to yordamida ko‘rsating. Gaplarni katta harf bilan boshlang.
checklistUz: Xonalar soni “There are ...“ bilan aytilgan.
Sevimli xona tanlanib, undagi kamida uch narsa sanalgan.
Kamida uch xil joy predlogi ishlatilgan (in / on / under / next to).
Kamida bitta inkor gap bor (there isn’t / there aren’t).
Gaplar katta harf bilan boshlanib, nuqta bilan tugatilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Bitta narsa borligini aytish uchun “There is ...“ kerak.
Ko‘p narsa borligini aytish uchun “There are ...“ kerak.
Narsa joyini ko‘rsatish uchun predloglar (masalan “under“) albatta kerak.

writing.modelAnswerEn: My home is a flat in Tashkent. There are four rooms: a living room, two bedrooms and a kitchen. My favourite room is my bedroom. There is a bed, a desk and a small lamp in it. My books are on the desk and my shoes are under the bed. There isn’t a TV in my room. I like my flat because it is quiet and clean.

writing.promptEn: Write a message to a friend. Tell them what food you have at home, what you don’t have, and what you like cooking.
writing.instructionUz: Do‘stingizga inglizcha xabar yozing. Uyda qanday ovqat borligini “there is / there are some ...“ bilan ayting, nimasi yo‘qligini “there isn’t / there aren’t any ...“ bilan ko‘rsating va oshxonada nima qilishni yoqtirishingizni “I like ...ing“ bilan yozing.
checklistUz: Kamida ikki tasdiq gapda “some“ ishlatilgan.
Kamida bitta inkor yoki so‘roq gapda “any“ ishlatilgan.
“I like ...ing“ iborasi bilan bir faoliyat aytilgan.
Kamida besh ta ovqat yoki ichimlik so‘zi ishlatilgan.
Xabar salom bilan boshlanib, ism bilan tugatilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: Bor narsani aytish uchun “some“ kerak: There is some bread.
Yo‘q narsani aytish uchun inkor gapda “any“ kerak: There isn’t any milk.
Yoqtirgan faoliyat “like + -ing“ bilan yoziladi: I like cooking.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Dilnoza! On Saturday I want to cook lunch at my home. There is some rice and there are six eggs in the fridge. There is also some bread and there are five apples in the bag. There isn’t any cheese and there aren’t any tomatoes. I like cooking rice with meat, and my sister likes making salad. Can you come at one o’clock? We can eat together. Your friend, Bekzod.

writing.promptEn: Write an email to your friend about your weekend. What are you going to do on Saturday and Sunday, and what can you do well?
writing.instructionUz: Do‘stingizga inglizcha elektron xat yozing. Shanba va Yakshanba kunlari nima qilmoqchi ekankingizni “I am going to ...“ bilan ayting, yaxshi bilaadigan bir ikki ishingizni “I can ...“ bilan ko‘rsating va do‘stingizni biror ishga taklif qiling.
checklistUz: Xat salom bilan boshlanib, vidolashuv va ism bilan tugatilgan.

I can play football well, but I can’t play basketball. I can bring water and apples. Do you want to come? On Sunday I am going to ride a bike with my father in the hills. In the evening my cousin is going to play the guitar at our home. Write to me soon! Your friend, Sardor.

writing.promptEn: Write a message to a friend about a trip. Where were you, how did you travel, and how do you get there?
writing.instructionUz: Do‘stingizga inglizcha xabar yozing. Qayerda bo‘lganingizni “I was ... / We were ...“ bilan ayting, qanday transportda borganningizni ko‘rsating va o‘sha yerga qanday borish yo‘lini “Go straight ahead ... Turn left / right ...“ bilan tushuntiring. Kamida bitta rejangizni “I am going to ...“ bilan qo‘shib yozing.
checklistUz: Xabarda kamida ikkita “was / were“ bilan gap bor.
Transport turi aytilgan (by bus, by train, by metro).
Yo‘l ko‘rsatish iborasi qo‘llanilgan (Go straight ahead / Turn left / Turn right).
Biror joyning yaqin yoki uzoq ekanini aytilgan (near / far).
Xabar salom bilan boshlanib, ism bilan tugatilgan.

mustInclude.whyUz: O‘tgan kun qayerda bo‘lganingizni “I was / it was“ bilan aytiladi.
Sayohat mavzusida transport joyi (station) albatta kerak.
Yo‘l ko‘rsatish uchun “Go straight ahead“ iborasi talab qilinadi.

writing.modelAnswerEn: Hi Nilufar! Last weekend was great. On Saturday my family and I were at the railway station in Tashkent. We went to Samarkand by train, and the station was big and clean. On Sunday we wanted to see the museum. It was not far from the station. A man helped us: “Go straight ahead and turn left at the crossing. The museum is next to the blue gate.” The museum was old and very interesting. Next month I am going to visit Samarkand again. Write to me soon! Your friend, Sardor.

transcript.text: Hello, Dilnoza! This is Sardor. Are you free on Saturday?
Hi, Sardor! Yes, I am. What are you doing?
My family is going to the park for a picnic. Do you want to come?
That sounds great! What time do we meet?
Let's meet at nine o'clock, at the main gate of the park.
OK. I'm bringing fruit and water. Can your brother come too?
Yes, he can. He is making a cake for everyone on Friday evening.
Perfect! What's the weather like on Friday? Is it going to rain?
The radio says it will be sunny all weekend, so we're lucky.
Wonderful. See you on Saturday then. Goodbye, Sardor!
Bye, Dilnoza! See you at nine.

writingTask.promptEn: Write an email to your English teacher. Tell her: (1) what you did last weekend, (2) what you are doing now, (3) when you can have the next lesson.
writingTask.instructionUz: Ingliz tilida aniq, sodda gaplar bilan yozing. Kamida 40 so‘z. Reja: kirish — asosiy qism — yakun.
